# RQ1: How Secure Is the Code Generated by Copilot in GitHub Projects?
**In one sentence:** Of 733 tool-generated Python and JavaScript snippets scanned with CodeQL plus Bandit/ESLint and manually filtered, 27.3% (200) contained security weaknesses, averaging 3 weaknesses per vulnerable snippet and exceeding one weakness in over half of vulnerable snippets.
## Key points
- 733 snippets were collected (672 Copilot, 38 CodeWhisperer, 23 Codeium) across Python and JavaScript and scanned with two tools per language: CodeQL plus Bandit for Python and CodeQL plus ESLint for JavaScript.
- A snippet counted as vulnerable if at least one of the two tools flagged it, after manual filtering that kept only results marked 1 and discarded Code-label findings not traceable to tool-generated code via preceding prompt comments.
- Two authors filtered independently over two weeks with Cohen's Kappa 0.85 (Repository label) and 0.82 (Code label), both above 0.8, then aggregated the kept results to count snippets with weaknesses.
- 200 of 733 snippets (27.3%) contained security weaknesses: 124 of 419 Python snippets (29.5%) and 76 of 314 JavaScript snippets (24.2%).
- 102 of the 200 vulnerable snippets (over half; 13.9% of all 733) had more than one security issue: 65 Python (15.5%) and 37 JavaScript (11.8%).
- 628 total security weaknesses were found in the 200 snippets (387 in Python, 241 in JavaScript), averaging ~3 per snippet regardless of language, with a maximum of 22 weaknesses in a single 1,595-LoC snippet.
- Per-snippet distributions (Fig. 13): Python mean 3.12 / median 2.00 / max 22 / std 3.79; JavaScript mean 3.17 / median 1.00 / max 19 / std 4.13; combined mean 3.14 / median 2.00 / max 22 / std 3.91 (all min 1.00).
---
## Approach
**Covers:** Section 4.1 RQ1, Approach (collection, scanning, and filtering)

- Collected 733 Python and JavaScript snippets generated by Copilot and two other tools from GitHub projects: 672 from Copilot, 38 from CodeWhisperer, and 23 from Codeium.
- Scanned with two static analysis tools per language (CodeQL + Bandit for Python; CodeQL + ESLint for JavaScript) for better coverage; a snippet was considered vulnerable as long as one tool detected a weakness.
- Filtered results per Section 3.3.2: Repository-label results marked 1 (weakness exists) or 0 (none); Code-label results marked 1 (weakness exists) or 0 (no weakness, or the weak snippet was not generated by code generation tools).
- Manual Code-label check required identifying whether the flagged code was auto-generated from the comment (prompt message) before the method; Fig. 11 working example: Line 149 in `aggregation.py` had a weakness and a Copilot prompt above it, so marked "1"; Line 145 in `_lytools.py` had a weakness but no prompt indicating Copilot generation, so marked "0" and discarded.
- Two authors independently filtered over two weeks, discussing unsure/disagreed cases to agreement; Cohen's Kappa was 0.85 (Repository label) and 0.82 (Code label), both higher than 0.8; kept only results marked 1 and aggregated multi-tool results; all labeling results are in the online replication package [21].

## Results
**Covers:** Section 4.1 RQ1, Results (Table 4; Fig. 12; Fig. 13)

- Table 4 statistics of snippets with security weaknesses:

| Language | # Snippets | # Security weaknesses | # Snippets containing security weaknesses | # containing more than one security weakness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Python | 419 | 387 | 124 (29.5%) | 65 (15.5%) |
| JavaScript | 314 | 241 | 76 (24.2%) | 37 (11.8%) |
| Total | 733 | 628 | 200 (27.3%) | 102 (13.9%) |

- Out of 733 generated snippets, 27.3% contained security weaknesses: around 30% of Python (124 of 419) and around 25% of JavaScript (76 of 314).
- More than half of the snippets containing weaknesses (102 of 200) have more than one security issue.
- Fig. 12 presents the distribution of application domains for the 200 snippets (27.3%) with weaknesses, split into (a) Python and (b) JavaScript.
- 628 security weaknesses were found in the 200 snippets; one snippet may contain multiple weaknesses attributed to multiple CWEs.
- Fig. 13 distribution of weaknesses per snippet: average incidence of 3 per snippet irrespective of language; maximum 22 in a single snippet of 1,595 LoC.
- Fig. 13 detail: Python — Median 2.00, Mean 3.12, Min 1.00, Max 22.00, Std Dev 3.79; JavaScript — Median 1.00, Mean 3.17, Min 1.00, Max 19.00, Std Dev 4.13; Python+JavaScript — Median 2.00, Mean 3.14, Min 1.00, Max 22.00, Std Dev 3.91.
- Note: the chunk tail spills into Section 4.2 RQ2's opening (CWE classification approach, including the Bandit CWE-78 vs CWE-427 remapping example), which belongs to chunk 09 and is not covered here beyond this note.
